scope: Bounded review of ISO 32000-2:2020(E) §8.6.6.3–.5 and relevant EC3 annotations: Indexed, Separation, DeviceN/NChannel. This does not certify all clause 8.6 colour conversion, output-device colourant availability, clause 10.8.3 rendering, printing behavior, malformed-input recovery, or every attribute in Tables 70–72.

source.page_rule: PDF physical page = ISO printed page + 15; sampled footers identify ISO 32000-2:2020(E). Where EC3 changes normative text, the StrikeOut/Caret annotation pair controls over the plain-text extraction.

rows.coverage: Colorants key/name consistency, NChannel process mapping and simulation, None, spot curves, multi-plane and archival consumers; full names are in the ledger row.

ledger.round_inventory: doc/reviews/2038-specification-audit/clause-inventory.json still lists all three review states as pending with no current artifacts.

requirements_sampled: Four-element Indexed form; base can be device/CIE or Separation/DeviceN but not Pattern/Indexed; hival <=255 and lookup has m*(hival+1) bytes are producer constraints.
Selecting Indexed initializes colour to index 0; each sample is an index; lookup bytes scale into each base component's range, bytes are consecutive by entry.
For operator values, real index rounds nearest with exact 0.5 up; values outside [0,hival] are adjusted to nearest endpoint.
assertions: crates/pdf-colour/src/colour.rs::an_indexed_space_reads_its_table checks a green entry and high clamp (direct unit).
crates/pdf-model/tests/indexed_out_of_range.rs::an_out_of_range_index_is_adjusted_to_the_nearest_entry checks negative/high values and 6.5 up, but its optional corpus file causes skip when absent.
crates/pdf-model/tests/dct_components.rs::an_indexed_space_over_a_jpeg_reads_the_sample_as_an_index is a public DCT image consumer.
drafts/indexed_rounding_initial.rs is a self-contained public exact-xref test of implicit index 0, 0.49, 0.5 and endpoint controls (draft only).
drafts/indexed_lab_lookup.rs is public exact-xref Lab byte scaling plus direct Lab control (draft only).
features.assessment: The read/lookup and integer/tie/clamp rules have direct code assertions; raster consumer tests cover image samples. Existing operator tie test depends on an optional corpus witness, so the self-contained exact-xref draft preserves the independently derived two-entry palette discriminator. Parser accepts producer-invalid hival/lookup shapes without validation; no normative reader-rejection rule was inferred.

requirements_sampled: Four-element Separation; single tint [0,1], subtractive convention; initial value 1.

All applies collectively to available colourants and complements tint on additive output; None produces no output. Reader must support these on any output, ignoring alternate/function although valid parameter values must still be provided.
On additive displays, a normal Separation always uses alternate and tint transform; direct colourant availability is for subtractive output. Alternate must be device/CIE, not special.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/tests/colour_paths.rs::the_none_colourant_marks_nothing uses a valid Separation and preserves green background.
crates/pdf-model/tests/colour_paths.rs::the_all_colourant_is_a_complemented_tint uses valid parameters and expected grayscale endpoints/tint complement.
drafts/special_space_initial_tints.rs publicly checks initial tint 1 with explicit full/zero controls (draft only).
features.assessment: The substantive additive-device consumer path (alternate tint transformation) and special All/None behavior are discriminated. `a_special_colourant_does_not_need_a_readable_tint_transform` is malformed-input tolerance only and is not counted as conformance evidence; valid All/None transform-ignore evidence exists in other tests. Direct selected-space public initial tint is absent in current tests; draft supplies one and a tint-zero control.

features.source_location: printed pp.203–211 / physical pp.218–226; Table 70 starts printed p.206 / physical p.221; Tables 71–72 at printed pp.208–209 / physical pp.223–224
requirements_sampled: DeviceN names define ordered input arity; names are unique except repeatable None; All is forbidden; reserved CMYK process names. DeviceN values are subtractive tints; selecting the space initializes all components to 1.

On additive devices unavailable colors use alternate/tint transform; NChannel has Subtype NChannel and per-component alternate route; DeviceN or omitted Subtype keeps prior behavior. Table 70 requires Colorants entries for all NChannel spot colorants; each key maps to a Separation naming that same colourant. Table 71 maps Components to corresponding process-space components. At most one process space; process component order and natural values apply. CMYK may be a subset/order; non-CMYK names follow process order. Tables 70–72 provide optional mixing information and may be ignored.

All-None DeviceN always discards; a None component in a reverting DeviceN passes its tint to transform. EC3 #309 changes the producer rule: None shall not be used in NChannel; this is a writer constraint, not a reader rejection rule.
code: crates/pdf-colour/src/colour/separation.rs::parse_separation (special names, all-None, simulation, process, transform order)
assertions: ::a_devicen_passes_its_none_components_to_the_tint_transform checks a valid plain DeviceN transform and asymmetric input order.
::an_nchannel_process_space_answers_without_a_readable_tint_transform is malformed-transform tolerance, not proof that invalid producer data is conforming.
drafts/special_space_initial_tints.rs checks public full-tint initial values against explicit controls (draft only).
features.assessment: Table 71 process routing and Table 70 key/name constraints have independent public/consumer assertions. None in NChannel is prohibited for writers after EC3 #309; the existing None-pass assertion is plain DeviceN. Table72 mixing hints may be ignored. The API/default distinction for NChannel spot-component evaluation is an accepted user-authorized policy under ADR 1229; simulation is available when requested. This does not certify the whole clause or all host integrations.
